newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: WMC POSTS A$69 MLN ABNORMAL PROFIT.
newsitem.headline: WMC POSTS A$69 MLN ABNORMAL PROFIT.

text.p: Gold and base metals miner WMC Ltd said on Wednesday it has posted an abnormal profit after tax of A$69 million in the year to June 30, due largely to a A$188.2 million after tax profit from the sale of the group's petroleum assets.
The petroleum assets sale profit was offset by a charge of A$63.8 million for redundant assets linked with the Olympic Dam expansion and redundant diesel powered generating assets.
There was also a A$18.3 million writedown after tax of gold assets to their recoverable value based on the recent gold price fall and an uncertain short term outlook, WMC said.
The carrying value of the Nifty copper operations were also written down by A$22.4 million because of lower recoveries.
There was a A$10.1 million after tax write-off because of change to the accounting practice for the amortisation of mine development at the Perserverance and Cox open pit mines.
WMC posted an equity profit after tax and abnormals of A$297.2 million, down 23 percent from the A$386.2 million posted in 1995/96.

Equity profit after tax, but before abnormals, was A$228.2 million, down 40.9 percent on the previous year and just in the upper end of the analysts' forecast range of A$195 million to A$240 million. WMC declared a seven cent final dividend, down from 11 cents the previous year.
WMC managing director Hugh Morgan said weaker metal prices across WMC's full product range significantly affected the result and some costs rose.

"The flash furnace roof collapse at the Kalgoorlie Nickel Smelter and reduced smelter availability associated with the commissioning of the expanded acid plant at Olympic Dam were the prime cause of the increased unit costs," Morgan said in a statement.
WMC said the company's balance sheet remained in a sound position to fund the current capital projects without having to access equity markets.
WMC's shares were up two cents at A$7.44 by 1.40 p.m. (0340 GMT).
